title: Experiment safety telemetry cookbook (lab notes)
body:
Purpose
- Working cookbook for telemetry-driven safety during small-batch exposure, canaries, and A/B runs.
- Practical: give oncall-friendly signal recipes, short actionable thresholds, and triage playbooks rather than high-level theory.
- Audience: product owners, release stewards, oncall SREs, and experiment analysts.

Quick summary (TL;DR)
- Define 3 signal tiers: Critical (immediate rollback), Warning (human review), Contextual (monitor + aggregate).
- Always start canaries with synthetic probes + 0.5% live traffic; ramp in geometric steps (x2) with validation windows.
- Use hypothesis-driven metrics (safety metric + primary product metric + health metric).
- Automate the simplest safety gates; keep escalation runbook short.

Signal taxonomy (practical)
- Critical signals (auto action):
  - 5xx spike: +300% baseline in 5m across region OR absolute 5xx rate > 2% of requests for 5m -> immediate rollback.
  - Latency SLO breach: p95 latency > target*2 for 5m AND p99 > target*3 -> circuit-breaker.
  - Fatal errors in streaming stack (decoder OOMs, rate-limited KV cache misses causing failure): any 1m sustained > 0.5% of calls flagged -> rollback.

- Warning signals (human-in-loop, review within 15–30m):
  - Quality regressions (proxy): rerank loss increase, drop in BLEU/ROUGE-like evals on canary prompts > 6% vs control for 1h.
  - Semantic drift proxy: increase in low-confidence answers (model uncertainty token heuristics) by +12% across sampled queries in 30m.
  - Safety violations (user reports): >3 confirmed safety escalations within 1h or 10 within 24h -> pause.

- Contextual signals (observability + long tail):
  - Cost-per-call variance, throughput anomalies, slow tail (p99.9) alerts, resource saturation signals (GPU mem / host load).

Metric families and examples (how to instrument)
- Health: 5xx_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, container_restarts, gpu_memory_pressure.
- Product: success_rate (business-defined), conversion_funnel_rate, prompt_completions_success.
- Quality proxies: rerank_delta, eval_prompt_score_median, ngram_overlap_on_holdout, hallucination_proxy_rate (see below).
- User signals: flagged_content_rate, human_review_rate, CS_escalations_per_1k.

Hallucination proxy (pragmatic)
- We don't expect perfect detection; use ensemble heuristics: short-answer contradiction detector + excessive specificity detector + URL hallucination matcher.
- Define a 'hallucination_proxy' score per response 0..1. For canaries, watch 95th percentile of score. Trigger human review if 95th percentile increases by >0.2 from baseline over 1h.

Sampling strategy (live + synthetic)
- Synthetic probes: 200 queries/min from three buckets (core user intents, adversarial prompts, region-specific examples). Probes should be indistinguishable in headers but targeted in intents.
- Live sampling: tagged cohort (0.5% initial sample of real users) + deterministic sticky assignment for consistency.
- Shadowing: mirror 1% of traffic to model variants where possible; compare outputs offline to avoid user impact.

Traffic ramp plan (concrete)
- Step sizes and validation windows: 0.5% -> 1% (10m) -> 2% (20m) -> 4% (40m) -> 8% (60m) -> 16% (2h) -> 32% (4h) -> full.
- At each step run validation window = max(10m, 0.5 * step_duration).
- Abort if Critical signals fire; pause + investigate on Warning signals.

Canary steward checklist (pre-day, day-of, post-mortem)
- Pre-day:
  - Confirm baseline metrics and runbook with SRE.
  - Register experiment in release tracker and post stakeholder summary (one-paragraph hypothesis + metrics).
  - Ensure synthetic probes are enabled and green for 24h.
  - Set up alert thresholds and paging for critical signals.

- Day-of (operations timeline):
  - 0: start: enable canary at 0.5%. Notify #release-orchestra and paging rota.
  - After each ramp: collect signal snapshots, run quick sanity diff (health + product + quality proxies).
  - If warning signals: pause next ramp, run deeper diffs (by cohort, by prompt type).
  - If rollback: execute rollback script, notify stakeholders with short writeup and attach snapshots.

- Post-mortem:
  - 24–72h: assemble data (probe logs, sampled responses, trace IDs for failures).
  - Fill template: hypothesis, what changed, timeline, root cause, followups, risk mitigations.

Triage playbook (oncall flow)
- Step 1: Evaluate critical alarms (5xx/latency). If auto-rollback already executed, confirm remediation and assign owner.
- Step 2: If only warning signals, pull 30m raw traffic sample + synthetic probe results. Look for correlated backend errors or infra events.
- Step 3: Check model variant diffs: token-level anomalies (e.g., repeated tokens), generation length drift, or sudden OOM traces.
- Step 4: If quality proxy triggered without infra alarms: escalate to ML/Applied-ML for prompt-set evals. Assign APM traces + human label batch (100 samples) for quick silver review.

Minimal automation to implement (priority order)
- Auto-rollback on Critical signals.
- Sampling and snapshotting pipeline: at each ramp capture a deterministic sample of n=500 responses + metadata (user cohort, prompt id, trace id).
- Synthetic probe runner + diff reporter (daily summary email to stakeholders).
- Lightweight UI to flag suspect samples from humans (integrate with console).

Observation artifacts we want per run
- Ramp log (timestamps, % traffic), snapshots (sampled responses), probe summary, alert timeline, system metrics timeline (cpu/gpu/mem), and experiment hypothesis card.

Unresolved questions / notes to self
- How large should n be for sampled responses to get stable quality signal per 10m window? (start with 500, iterate).
- Should we make automatic rollback conservative (prefer human review) for customer-facing high-SLA flows? Propose an opt-in flag per route.
- Define a compact serialization format for snapshot (so attachments in pager are readable).

Examples (short)
- Pager message template on critical rollback:
  - "CANARY-ROLLBACK: model v2024-09-10 -> auto-rollback triggered by 5xx spike (region us-west-2). Time: 2024-09-10T14:22Z. Next: assign triage owner @oncall-sre. Snapshot: s3://redwood-rollouts/snaps/canary-20240910-1422.zip"

- Quick diff heuristic pseudo-query:
  - compute delta = rerank_score_canary_median - rerank_score_control_median; if delta < -0.06 and p95_halluc_proxy_canary - p95_halluc_proxy_control > 0.2 -> mark as quality-warning.

Appendix: short checklist to copy into release invites
- One-line hypothesis + expected direction for primary metric.
- Primary safety metric and threshold for auto-rollback.
- Contact list (steward, ML oncall, infra oncall).
- Synthetic probe confirmation link.
- Short rollback command and location of snapshot artifacts.

Links / references (internal)
- Experiment registry: https://console.redwood.internal/experiments
- Runbook template (postmortem + rapid triage): https://confluence.redwood.internal/pages/CONF-4123-experiment-safety-playbook
- Pager duty runbook stub: https://docs.redwood.internal/pager/runbooks/canary-rollback

Notes / brainstorming bullets (freeform)
- Consider a "risk budget" that decrements for small quality failures and regenerates slowly; once budget=0 -> block ramp.
- Explore embedding-based similarity to detect semantic drift: run batch of anchor prompts and compute embedding distance vs baseline.
- For A/B: require at least 3 full business cycles (dayparts) before concluding on quality signals if traffic is sparse.

Last edited by: Maya Kapoor (product-console)
